answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to earn a small, nontransferable reputation stake through completed jobs that counterparties verify, then weight access to valuable tasks by that record. A Sybil attacker can still create many accounts, but cannot cheaply give them credible histories: each must complete real work and risk losing its stake after fraud. A thread of verified jobs becomes a beacon through the nebula of new accounts, making fabricated identities costly rather than impossible.
